qt: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:

In its answer to the question for written answer E-002794/2026(ASW)1, the Commission stated: ‘The Commission did not call for vaccination to be mandatory. The organisation and delivery of health services and medical care is a national competence. As such, decisions about vaccines […] are the sole responsibility of the Member States.’ This is incorrect, as the Commission was primarily responsible for the COVID-19 vaccination campaign. It negotiated and signed the vaccine contracts with the pharmaceutical companies, in which it accepted that their efficacy and side effects were not known. The WHO, an integral part of EU legislation since 2013 (Decision 1082/2013/EU), established criteria for mandatory vaccination on 13 April 2021. On 8 September 2021, the prerequisites for and experiences with mandatory vaccination for the general population and for specific occupational groups were discussed in the presence of the Commission, WHO, Member States and various EU institutions. And on the 1 December 2021, the President of the Commission called for mandatory vaccination across the EU to be considered. 1.
Why is the Commission now distancing itself from its leading coordinating role in the COVID-19 vaccination campaign and mandatory vaccination?
Why is the Commission now declaring that health is a national competence, while for years it has been taking on more and more health competences?

Was, and is, the Commission for or against the various mandatory COVID-19 vaccination schemes adopted in the individual Member States – for instance, for certain occupational groups or for the general population, as in Austria?
